identity.name: Ömer Faruk Dolanbay
identity.tagline: I build the coordination layer — the part that decides which agent speaks next, and why.

agents.label: orchestrator
body: I build **multi-agent systems** — specifically the coordination layer: routing, handoff, and the rules that decide which agent runs next and when the whole thing should stop.

The interesting failures are almost never in the model. They are in the seams. An agent answers confidently from context it should have rejected. A planner hands off work it already finished. A loop runs because nobody defined a termination condition. Swapping in a stronger model hides those for a while; it does not fix any of them.

So most of what I build runs on **small models, locally** — Foundry Local, no API key, nothing leaving the machine. The constraint is deliberate. When you cannot escalate your way out of a bad handoff, the orchestration has to actually be correct.

agents.label: researcher
body: A confident agent on top of bad context is worse than no agent — it produces a wrong answer with a reasoning trace attached. So a large share of my work sits *below* the agent layer, where the context is decided.

Chunking that survives Turkish morphology. NER-based anonymisation, so personal data is removed before a model ever sees it. And evaluation harnesses, because without one you cannot tell whether a change helped or simply relocated the error.

projects.title: Foundry Local Agentic RAG
projects.blurb: A Turkish assistant that escalates through three coordination strategies — plain RAG, then agentic RAG, then multi-agent — so the cost of coordination is only paid when the question needs it. Runs entirely offline on small models via Microsoft Foundry Local.

projects.title: Multi-Agent Decision Support System
projects.blurb: University administrative processes handled as an agent pipeline — intake, routing, drafting, review — rather than one prompt attempting all four and doing none of them well.

projects.title: Claude Usage Bar
projects.blurb: Live Claude usage quota pinned to the Windows 11 taskbar. Small, but I look at it more often than anything else I have written.

projects.title: Turkish NER Text Anonymizer
projects.blurb: Named-entity recognition tuned for Turkish, used as a scrubbing stage so personal data is stripped before it reaches a model at all.

projects.title: Rating-Based DAG System
projects.blurb: Airflow DAGs over PostgreSQL where scheduling priority follows a rating signal instead of a fixed cron — the scheduler decides what matters next.
